title: On-Policy Delta Distillation
hook: Instead of copying a teacher's raw outputs, this method distills only the *change* reasoning-tuning made — a sharper signal that beats standard on-policy distillation across math, science, and code.
key_points: Defines the 'delta signal': the difference between a reasoning-tuned teacher and its own pre-reasoning-tuning base model, rather than imitating the teacher's output distribution directly.
The delta signal isolates the specific change reasoning tuning made, giving a more targeted supervision signal for transferring reasoning ability.
Method is called On-Policy Delta Distillation (OPD²): the student still generates its own tokens on-policy, but is scored against this delta rather than the raw teacher.
Consistently beats conventional on-policy distillation on math, science, and code-reasoning benchmarks, reaching strong performance with a short post-training run.
content_html: On-policy distillation lets a student model learn from a teacher's token-level judgments on its own generations, sidestepping some of the constraints reward models impose in standard reinforcement learning post-training. But despite growing use, the basic design choice of what signal to distill had been underexplored.
extra_html:
Byeongho Heo and colleagues at NAVER AI Lab propose distilling a different target: the delta signal, defined as the difference between the reasoning-tuned teacher and its own base model from before instruction/reasoning tuning. Rather than asking the student to imitate the teacher's full output distribution, On-Policy Delta Distillation (OPD²) scores the student's own on-policy generations against this delta — a signal that isolates specifically what reasoning tuning changed, instead of the teacher's whole behavior.

Across math, science, and code-reasoning benchmarks, the authors report OPD² consistently beating conventional on-policy distillation, and reaching strong reasoning performance after only a short post-training run. Code is planned for release at github.com/naver-ai/opd2. Source: arXiv, arxiv.org/abs/2607.15161.

related.title: On the Geometry of On-Policy Distillation
related.hook: On-policy distillation isn't a midpoint between fine-tuning and RL — it carves its own narrow path through parameter space, locking into a low-dimensional subspace early in training.

related.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
related.hook: RL post-training gets pricier as models scale, since it needs the strong model's own rollouts. Direct-OPD reuses a cheap RL run on a small model instead, transferring the direction RL moved it.

related.title: Trust Region On-Policy Distillation
related.hook: On-policy distillation breaks when teacher and student disagree too much. TrOPD only trusts the teacher where its supervision is reliable — and skips the rest.

related.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
related.hook: A big model's softened probabilities say more than hard labels - they reveal how classes relate, so training a small model to mimic them transfers knowledge a one-hot target never could.

flashcards.prompt: What is the 'delta signal' in On-Policy Delta Distillation (OPD²)?
flashcards.back_html: The difference between a reasoning-tuned teacher model and its own base model before reasoning tuning — capturing specifically what reasoning tuning changed, rather than the teacher's full output distribution.

flashcards.prompt: Why might distilling the delta signal transfer reasoning ability better than imitating the teacher's raw outputs?

choices.text: It isolates the specific change reasoning tuning induced, giving a more direct and targeted supervision signal
It requires no teacher model at all, only the base model
It removes the need for on-policy student generations entirely

flashcards.explanation_html: Standard on-policy distillation imitates everything about the teacher's distribution; the delta signal narrows that down to just the reasoning-specific change, which the paper shows transfers more effectively.

flashcards.prompt: How does OPD² compare to conventional on-policy distillation across math, science, and code-reasoning benchmarks?
flashcards.back_html: OPD² consistently outperforms conventional on-policy distillation, letting reasoning LLMs reach strong performance after only a short post-training period.
